item.statement_excerpt:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, and let $J(s,t,x)$ be a smooth family of almost complex structures on $X$, defined for $(s,t)$ in an open subset $U\subset\mathbb R^2$. Suppose the norms of $J$ and its derivatives through total order two, using the Levi-Civita connection in $X$ and ordinary derivatives in $s,t$, are uniformly bounded. Then there are constants $a,b\ge0$, depending only on these bounds and $g$, such that every smooth solution
$$u_s+J(s,t,u)u_t=0$$
has energy density $e=(|u_s|_g^2+|u_t|_g^2)/2$ satisfying
$$\Delta e\ge-ae^2-be.$$
Consequently there are $r_0,\varepsilon_0>0$ depending only on the same data such that, whenever $\overline B_r(z)\subset U$, $0<r\le r_0$, and $\int_{B_r(z)}e<\varepsilon_0$, one has
$$|du(z)|_g^2\le\frac{32}{3\pi r^2}\int_{B_r(z)}e.$$
These are interior estimates for smooth actual solutions. No boundary estimate or higher-derivative compactness is asserted.

Let $H=|\nabla du|$ and $P=|du|$. Differentiating the last expression for $\tau$ in a source direction gives a uniform bound $$|\nabla\tau|\le c\bigl(P^3+P^2+P+(P+1)H\bigr).$$ For example differentiation of $Q(v,v)$ gives terms with coefficient derivatives times $|v|^2$, bounded by $c(P+1)P^2$, and terms bounded by $cPH$; differentiation of $Rv$ gives terms bounded by $c(P+1)P+cH$. This accounts for every source derivative, including the explicit domain dependence of $J$. A single $c$ works for all maps because its ingredients are the fixed tensor bounds. [step 1.1, algebra]

The needed energy identity follows by metric compatibility and commuting covariant derivatives. For source indices $\alpha, eta\in\{s,t\}$, first differentiate $e= rac12\sum_\alpha\langle u_\alpha,u_\alphaangle$ twice to obtain $\Delta e=H^2+\sum_{\alpha, eta}\langle
abla_ eta
abla_ eta u_\alpha,u_\alphaangle$. Torsion-freeness replaces $
abla_ eta u_\alpha$ by $
abla_\alpha u_ eta$, and commuting the remaining derivatives replaces their sum by $
abla_\alpha	au$ plus curvature terms $R^X(u_ eta,u_\alpha)u_ eta$, with a sign determined by the curvature convention and irrelevant to the estimate. Compactness bounds their absolute contribution by $c_1P^4$. Thus $$\Delta e\ge H^2-|
abla	au|P-c_1P^4.$$ Using step 2.1 and $P^3\le(P^4+P^2)/2$, this is bounded below by $H^2-c_2(P^4+P^2)-c_3(P^2+P)H$. Finally $c_3(P^2+P)H\le H^2/2+c_4(P^4+P^2)$ by the elementary square inequality. Discard the remaining nonnegative $H^2/2$ and use $P^2=2e$ to obtain $\Delta e\ge-ae^2-be$ for uniform $a,b\ge0$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

Set $r_0=1/\sqrt{\max\{b,1\}}$ and $\varepsilon_0=3\pi/(128\max\{a,1\})$. Then $r\le r_0$ implies $br^2\le1$, and $\int e<\varepsilon_0$ implies $a\int e<3\pi/64$. Smoothness makes $e$ a nonnegative $C^2$ function on a neighborhood of the closed disk. Apply [F1] to step 3.1 and multiply its conclusion by two, since $|du(z)|^2=2e(z)$. This proves the gradient bound, with constants independent of the chosen solution and disk. [F1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎
